legend: The lesions are located in sun-exposed areas (shown here) and non–sun-exposed areas. The skin exhibits a papulovesicular eruption. Many of the lesions are ulcerated, with haemorrhagic crust and pitted scars.

Panniculitic form. In severe cases the lymphoid infiltrate is dense and diffuse, involving the dermis, subcutaneous tissue, and muscle. The atypical infiltrate surrounds blood vessels, with angiodestructive features.

The lymphoid infiltrate predominates in the dermis. The infiltrate is mainly located around adnexa and blood vessels. There is an intraepidermal spongiotic vesiculation. The lymphoid infiltrate, which can be of T-cell or NK-cell lineage, is composed of small to medium-sized cells without atypia. The lymphoid cells are positive for EBV, as demonstrated by in situ hybridization for EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER).
